answer: Time-locked resource contribution. Each identity must contribute a verifiable minimum of a scarce non-financial resource—such as distinct saffron supply-chain provenance records—before it can act. A validator checks this signal before minting the identity. To scale sybils, an attacker must independently source that many genuine records, and the atlas of known provenance is audited, so duplicates get rejected. The concrete cost is the sourcing effort per identity.
